description: Follows anomalous Pacific tropical convection through latent heating and atmospheric waves to seasonal rain and storm-track odds in the Americas, Australia, Indonesia, India and the Atlantic.

related_resources.reason: Original coupled Pacific SST/trade-wind/Southern Oscillation argument and remote winter circulation correlations.
Rainfall composites from more than 1,700 stations; identifies coherent yet probabilistic seasonal associations.
Empirical winter geopotential-height teleconnection patterns, including the Pacific-North American structure.
Conditional regional rainfall and jet-stream impacts, ecological and US seasonal tendencies; not deterministic local forecasts.
Increased Atlantic tropical cyclone vertical wind shear in El Niño, with other factors affecting seasonal hurricane numbers.
Region-specific indices: Niño 3.4, Southern Oscillation, ocean-atmosphere multivariate approaches.

parts of Indonesia and Australia are more likely to experience suppressed rainfall

two El Niño episodes with similar central-Pacific temperature indices may have distinct effects

background: Introduces latent-heat release, atmospheric Rossby waves, seasonal composites and probabilistic impact statements without assumed meteorological training.
